title: Psalms Chapter 92 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 92 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 92 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 92.

questions.question: What is described as a good thing to do in Psalms 92:1?
options: To give thanks unto the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: To give thanks unto the LORD
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'It is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD...' indicating that giving thanks is encouraged.

questions.question: What should be shown forth in the morning according to Psalms 92:2?
questions.correctAnswer: Lovingkindness
questions.explanation: The verse specifies, 'To shew forth thy lovingkindness in the morning...' highlighting the need to display God's lovingkindness.

questions.question: What instruments are mentioned in Psalms 92:3?
questions.correctAnswer: Psaltery and harp
questions.explanation: The verse lists, 'Upon an instrument of ten strings, and upon the psaltery; upon the harp...' which specifies these instruments.

questions.question: Who has made the psalmist glad according to Psalms 92:4?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: The text states, 'For thou, LORD, hast made me glad through thy work...' indicating that the LORD is the source of gladness.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 92:5 states that the LORD's works are great.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse explicitly says, 'O LORD, how great are thy works!' confirming that the works of the LORD are indeed great.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 92:6, a fool understands the deep thoughts of the LORD.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'A brutish man knoweth not; neither doth a fool understand this.' indicating that fools do not understand God's thoughts.

questions.question: What happens to the wicked according to Psalms 92:7?
options: They shall be destroyed for ever
They will prosper in their ways
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be destroyed for ever
questions.explanation: The verse mentions, 'When the wicked spring as the grass... it is that they shall be destroyed for ever,' indicating their ultimate fate.

questions.question: Who is referred to as most high in Psalms 92:8?
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'But thou, LORD, art most high for evermore,' clearly identifying the LORD as the most high.

questions.question: What will happen to the enemies of the LORD according to Psalms 92:9?
questions.correctAnswer: They shall perish
questions.explanation: The verse indicates, 'For, lo, thine enemies shall perish...' signifying that the enemies of the LORD will not endure.

questions.question: What does the psalmist say shall be exalted like the horn of an unicorn in Psalms 92:10?
questions.correctAnswer: My horn
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'But my horn shalt thou exalt like the horn of an unicorn...' referring to the psalmist's strength.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 92:11 expresses that the psalmist will desire to see his enemies defeated.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Mine eye also shall see my desire on mine enemies...' indicating a desire for victory over enemies.

questions.question: In Psalms 92, which instruction comes FIRST?
questions.correctAnswer: To give thanks
questions.explanation: The first instruction in the chapter is to give thanks as stated in Psalms 92:1.

questions.question: What do the righteous flourish like in Psalms 92:12?
questions.correctAnswer: A palm tree
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'The righteous shall flourish like the palm tree...' comparing the righteous to a palm tree.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 92:14 mentions that the righteous will be fat and flourishing in old age.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The verse indicates, 'They shall still bring forth fruit in old age; they shall be fat and flourishing...' confirming this statement.

questions.question: What is said about the LORD in Psalms 92:15?
questions.correctAnswer: He is my rock
questions.explanation: The verse states, '...he is my rock, and there is no unrighteousness in him,' affirming that the LORD is a steadfast foundation.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 92 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 92 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 92:6, who does not understand the greatness of God's works and thoughts?
options: The brutish man and the fool
questions.correctAnswer: The brutish man and the fool
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:6 states that a brutish man knoweth not and neither doth a fool understand the greatness of God's works and thoughts, highlighting their lack of insight compared to the faithful.

questions.question: What does Psalms 92:7 say will ultimately happen to the wicked who flourish like grass?
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be destroyed forever
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:7 clearly teaches that although the wicked may flourish like grass for a time, they will be destroyed forever, emphasizing God's justice and final judgment.

questions.question: How does Psalms 92:8 describe the Lord in contrast to the wicked?
options: The Lord is most high forevermore
The Lord is weak and temporary
The Lord is silent in judgment
The Lord is hidden and unknown
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord is most high forevermore
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:8 contrasts the fleeting nature of the wicked with the eternal sovereignty of the Lord, who is described as most high forevermore.

questions.question: What promise is given in Psalms 92:9 regarding the Lord's enemies?
options: They shall perish and be scattered
questions.correctAnswer: They shall perish and be scattered
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:9 promises that the Lord's enemies, specifically the workers of iniquity, will perish and be scattered, affirming God's protection over the faithful.

questions.question: In Psalms 92:10, what is the significance of the horn like the horn of an unicorn being exalted?
options: It symbolizes strength and honor granted by God
It represents a physical horn used in worship
It means the psalmist will become a wild beast
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes strength and honor granted by God
questions.explanation: The horn is a biblical symbol of strength and power. Psalms 92:10 indicates that God will exalt the psalmist's horn like an unicorn's, meaning he will be given honor and strength by God.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 92:6, even a fool can understand the deep thoughts of God.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:6 explicitly states that a brutish man knoweth not and neither doth a fool understand the greatness of God's works and thoughts, indicating they do not comprehend God's ways.

questions.question: What does Psalms 92:7 teach us about the temporary nature of wickedness?
options: Wickedness may flourish briefly but will be destroyed forever
questions.correctAnswer: Wickedness may flourish briefly but will be destroyed forever
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:7 shows that although the wicked may spring up and flourish like grass, their success is temporary and they will be destroyed forever, teaching about the fleeting nature of evil.

questions.question: How does Psalms 92:8 encourage believers to view God's sovereignty?
options: God is uncertain in His rule
questions.correctAnswer: God is most high forevermore
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:8 affirms God's eternal sovereignty by declaring He is most high forevermore, encouraging believers to trust in His everlasting rule amid life's challenges.

questions.question: What practical lesson about faith can be drawn from the promise in Psalms 92:9 that enemies will perish?
options: Trust in God’s justice and protection against adversaries
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in God’s justice and protection against adversaries
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:9 assures believers that God's enemies will perish and be scattered, teaching us to trust God’s justice and protection rather than taking matters into our own hands.

questions.question: What does Psalms 92:10 suggest about the believer’s spiritual empowerment?
options: God will exalt the believer and anoint them with fresh oil
The believer will be left to struggle alone
The believer will lose strength over time
The believer must earn their own power
questions.correctAnswer: God will exalt the believer and anoint them with fresh oil
questions.explanation: According to Psalms 92:10, God will exalt the believer's horn like an unicorn’s and anoint them with fresh oil, symbolizing spiritual empowerment and divine blessing.

questions.question: How do Psalms 92:6 and Psalms 92:7 together teach about the contrast between the wise and the wicked?
options: The wise understand God’s works, but the wicked flourish only temporarily before destruction
The wicked always triumph over the wise
Both the wise and wicked flourish equally
Neither the wise nor wicked understand God's plans
questions.correctAnswer: The wise understand God’s works, but the wicked flourish only temporarily before destruction
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:6 shows that fools do not understand God's works, whereas Psalms 92:7 explains that though the wicked flourish like grass, they will be destroyed forever, teaching the ultimate victory of wisdom and righteousness.

questions.question: What does Psalms 92:9 imply will happen if we remain faithful despite opposition?
options: Our enemies will perish and be scattered
questions.correctAnswer: Our enemies will perish and be scattered
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:9 promises that the enemies of the Lord will perish and be scattered, encouraging believers to remain faithful and trust God in the face of opposition.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 92:10 teaches that God’s empowerment of the believer is temporary and fades quickly.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:10 emphasizes that God will exalt the believer and anoint them with fresh oil, symbolizing ongoing and renewing empowerment, not a temporary fading one.

questions.question: How might the promise in Psalms 92:10 about being anointed with fresh oil encourage a believer facing trials?
options: It assures that God will renew their strength and honor
It suggests they should avoid all challenges
It means they will not face any difficulties
questions.correctAnswer: It assures that God will renew their strength and honor
questions.explanation: The anointing with fresh oil in Psalms 92:10 symbolizes God's renewing blessing and strength, encouraging believers to trust God to sustain and honor them during trials.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 92:8, the Lord’s status as 'most high' is only for a limited time.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:8 states that the Lord is most high 'forevermore,' indicating His eternal and unchanging sovereignty, not a limited or temporary status.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 92 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 92.

questions.question: According to Psalms 92:11, what will the psalmist's eye and ears witness?
options: The desire fulfilled against enemies and the wicked
The joy of the morning light
questions.correctAnswer: The desire fulfilled against enemies and the wicked
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:11 states that the psalmist's eye shall see his desire on his enemies, and his ears shall hear his desire of the wicked that rise up against him, indicating victorious observation over adversaries.

questions.question: What simile is used in Psalms 92:12 to describe the righteous?
options: Like the palm tree and a cedar in Lebanon
Like a lily in the valley
questions.correctAnswer: Like the palm tree and a cedar in Lebanon
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:12 uses the similes of a flourishing palm tree and a growing cedar in Lebanon to depict the strength and flourishing condition of the righteous.

questions.question: According to Psalms 92:13, where do those who are planted flourish?
options: In the courts of the LORD’s house
questions.correctAnswer: In the courts of the LORD’s house
questions.explanation: The verse Psalms 92:13 states that those planted in the house of the LORD flourish in the courts of our God, emphasizing divine protection and blessing in God's presence.

questions.question: What does Psalms 92:14 say about the fruitfulness of the righteous in old age?
options: They still bring forth fruit and remain flourishing
questions.correctAnswer: They still bring forth fruit and remain flourishing
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:14 affirms that the righteous will continue to be productive and prosperous even in old age, symbolizing enduring vitality and blessing.

questions.question: What two attributes of the LORD are declared in Psalms 92:15?
options: He is upright and a rock without unrighteousness
questions.correctAnswer: He is upright and a rock without unrighteousness
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:15 declares the LORD as upright and a rock, emphasizing His righteousness and stability, with no unrighteousness found in Him.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of the righteous flourishing like a tree as in Psalms 92:12?
questions.correctAnswer: Jeremiah 17:7-8
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 17:7-8 similarly compares the blessed man to a tree planted by the waters that yields fruit in due season, echoing the flourishing righteous imagery of Psalms 92:12.

questions.question: The phrase 'my horn shalt thou exalt like the horn of an unicorn' in Psalms 92:10 uses 'horn' symbolically. What does this symbolize?
questions.correctAnswer: Strength and exaltation
questions.explanation: In Psalms 92:10, the 'horn' symbolizes strength, power, and honor, and its exaltation like the horn of a unicorn (a strong wild ox) represents being lifted up and empowered.

questions.question: In Psalms 92:9, what is said will happen to the LORD’s enemies?
options: They shall perish and be scattered
questions.correctAnswer: They shall perish and be scattered
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:9 declares that the LORD’s enemies and all workers of iniquity will perish and be scattered, showing ultimate divine judgment on the wicked.

questions.question: Which literary device best describes the structure of Psalms 92:7-9, where the wicked flourish temporarily but are ultimately destroyed?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasm
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:7-9 employs chiastic structure contrasting the temporary flourishing of the wicked with their ultimate destruction, creating a mirrored pattern reinforcing the message.

questions.question: The Hebrew word translated as 'flourish' in Psalms 92:12 and 13 most closely means:
questions.correctAnswer: To grow luxuriantly or prosper
questions.explanation: The Hebrew verb used in Psalms 92:12-13 for 'flourish' (yatsar) connotes vigorous growth and prosperity, reflecting vitality and divine blessing.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects the theme of God being the 'rock' and without unrighteousness as stated in Psalms 92:15?
questions.correctAnswer: 1 Corinthians 10:4
questions.explanation: 1 Corinthians 10:4 refers to Christ as the spiritual rock who provides living water, paralleling Psalms 92:15’s depiction of the LORD as a rock, symbolizing stability and righteousness.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 92:14 indicates that the righteous will lose their ability to produce fruit in old age.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:14 states the opposite; the righteous shall still bring forth fruit in old age and be fat and flourishing, showing continued productivity.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 92:6 suggests that fools understand the deep thoughts of God.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:6 clearly says a brutish man knows not, and a fool does not understand God's deep thoughts, indicating their lack of comprehension.

questions.question: Which Old Testament book contains a passage that thematically connects to the sabbath focus of Psalms 92:1?
questions.correctAnswer: Exodus 20:8-11
questions.explanation: Exodus 20:8-11 commands keeping the sabbath day holy, which connects to Psalms 92:1’s designation of this psalm as a song for the sabbath day.

questions.question: How does Psalms 92:10 foreshadow New Testament themes of anointing and empowerment?
options: By referencing the anointing with fresh oil symbolizing divine empowerment
By describing the building of a temple
By prophesying the destruction of enemies
questions.correctAnswer: By referencing the anointing with fresh oil symbolizing divine empowerment
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:10’s mention of anointing with fresh oil foreshadows New Testament themes where anointing signifies empowerment by the Holy Spirit, as seen in Acts 10:38.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 92 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 92 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 92:1 emphasize as a good thing to do on the sabbath day?
options: To give thanks unto the LORD and sing praises unto His name
questions.correctAnswer: To give thanks unto the LORD and sing praises unto His name
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:1 explicitly states that it is a good thing to give thanks unto the LORD and to sing praises unto His name on the sabbath day, highlighting worship as the appropriate response to God’s holiness.

questions.question: According to Psalms 92:2, what two attributes of God are to be shown forth morning and night?
questions.correctAnswer: Lovingkindness and faithfulness
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:2 commands the believer to show forth God's lovingkindness in the morning and His faithfulness every night, emphasizing God's steadfast covenantal love and reliability.

questions.question: What instruments are mentioned in Psalms 92:3 for praising God?
questions.correctAnswer: Ten-stringed instrument, psaltery, and harp
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:3 specifies praising God with an instrument of ten strings, upon the psaltery, and upon the harp with a solemn sound, indicating the importance of musical worship instruments in expressing reverence.

questions.question: What is the theological significance of the phrase in Psalms 92:5, 'O LORD, how great are thy works! and thy thoughts are very deep'?
options: It reveals God's omniscience and the inscrutability of His divine plans
It emphasizes human wisdom over divine plans
It teaches that God's works are limited and shallow
It shows God's indifference to creation
questions.correctAnswer: It reveals God's omniscience and the inscrutability of His divine plans
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:5 praises the greatness of God's works and the depth of His thoughts, which reveals His infinite wisdom and omniscience, doctrines foundational to Christian theology regarding God's nature (cf. Romans 11:33).

questions.question: What contrast does Psalms 92:6 draw between the brutish man and the wise understanding of God's works?
options: The brutish man does not know, and the fool does not understand God's works
The brutish man is wiser than the fool
The brutish man understands God's works better than the wise
Both brutish man and fool have perfect knowledge
questions.correctAnswer: The brutish man does not know, and the fool does not understand God's works
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:6 highlights human limitation, showing that brutish and foolish people fail to comprehend God's works and thoughts, emphasizing the necessity of divine revelation for true understanding.

questions.question: What eventual fate of the wicked is declared in Psalms 92:7?
options: They will be forgiven without repentance
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be destroyed forever
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:7 teaches that although the wicked flourish temporarily, they will ultimately be destroyed forever, affirming the doctrine of divine judgment and eternal separation from God (cf. Matthew 25:46).

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Psalms 92:8 where it says, 'But thou, LORD, art most high for evermore'?
questions.correctAnswer: God's eternal sovereignty
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:8 affirms God's eternal sovereignty and exalted position above all, a key attribute emphasizing His unchangeable reign throughout all ages (cf. Isaiah 46:10).

questions.question: What does Psalms 92:10 mean by 'my horn shalt thou exalt like the horn of an unicorn'?
options: It symbolizes strength and honor granted by God
It denotes an actual horned animal worship
It refers to human pride without God
It means losing power and dignity
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes strength and honor granted by God
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:10 uses the imagery of the horn of a unicorn (a symbol of strength and majesty) to depict God exalting the psalmist with strength and honor, illustrating divine empowerment and blessing.

questions.question: According to Psalms 92:12, what two trees symbolize the flourishing of the righteous, and what might this imply theologically?
options: Palm tree and cedar in Lebanon; symbolizing uprightness and longevity
Oak and willow; symbolizing fragility and sorrow
Pine and cypress; symbolizing death and mourning
Fig and olive; symbolizing fruitlessness and barrenness
questions.correctAnswer: Palm tree and cedar in Lebanon; symbolizing uprightness and longevity
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:12 likens the righteous to flourishing palm trees and cedars, indicating their spiritual vitality, uprightness, and enduring faith, consistent with biblical symbolism of growth and blessing.

questions.question: What does Psalms 92:14 teach about the vitality of the godly in old age?
options: They shall still bring forth fruit and be flourishing
They will become weak and unproductive
They will be forgotten by God
They will cease from all good works
questions.correctAnswer: They shall still bring forth fruit and be flourishing
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:14 promises that the godly remain fruitful and vigorous even in old age, illustrating sanctification and perseverance as ongoing processes empowered by God.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal teaching do Psalms 92:7 and Psalms 92:9 convey about the fate of the wicked?
options: They will be destroyed and scattered, confirming their ultimate judgment
They will be exalted and rewarded
questions.correctAnswer: They will be destroyed and scattered, confirming their ultimate judgment
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:7 and 92:9 together teach that although the wicked prosper temporarily, they will ultimately be destroyed and scattered, affirming the doctrine of final judgment and divine justice.

questions.question: How do Psalms 92:4 and Psalms 92:15 together reflect on God's role as Creator and Righteous Rock?
options: God's works bring joy and He is the unchanging foundation of righteousness
questions.correctAnswer: God's works bring joy and He is the unchanging foundation of righteousness
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:4 shows joy in God's creative work, while 92:15 declares God as the rock with no unrighteousness, highlighting both His creative providence and moral perfection as the foundation for believers’ trust.

questions.question: What theological insight do Psalms 92:11 and Psalms 92:10 provide about divine vindication against enemies?
options: God exalts the believer and grants them victory over their enemies
God allows enemies to triumph indefinitely
The believer must rely on personal strength alone
questions.correctAnswer: God exalts the believer and grants them victory over their enemies
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:10 speaks of exaltation like a horn, and 92:11 speaks of seeing and hearing desire against enemies, together indicating God’s vindication and empowerment of the righteous against opposition.

questions.question: Sceptics claim the prosperity of the wicked contradicts God's justice. What does Psalms 92:7-9 actually teach about this issue?
options: The wicked may flourish temporarily but will ultimately perish and be scattered
The wicked will always prosper without consequence
God ignores the deeds of the wicked
The wicked will be exalted by God
questions.correctAnswer: The wicked may flourish temporarily but will ultimately perish and be scattered
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:7-9 acknowledges the temporary flourishing of the wicked but affirms their ultimate destruction and scattering, underscoring God's righteous judgment and addressing the problem of apparent injustice.

questions.question: What doctrine is taught by Psalms 92:13-14 about the blessing of being 'planted in the house of the LORD'?
options: Sanctification and continual fruitfulness in the presence of God
questions.correctAnswer: Sanctification and continual fruitfulness in the presence of God
questions.explanation: Psalms 92:13-14 teach that those planted in God's house flourish and bear fruit even in old age, illustrating the ongoing sanctification and blessing experienced by the covenant community.
